record.original_question: Fix 0≤s≤r with r≥s for orientation-preserving C^r circle diffeomorphisms of irrational rotation number α. Determine exactly which irrational α have the property that every such C^r diffeomorphism is conjugate to the rotation R_α by a C^s diffeomorphism, and likewise determine the corresponding local class where the diffeomorphism is only assumed to be C^r-close to R_α. Are the global and local arithmetic classes different?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ denote the circle, and for $r\geq 1$ let $\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})$ denote the group of orientation-preserving $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, let $R_\alpha:\mathbb{T}\to\mathbb{T}$, $R_\alpha(x)=x+\alpha\pmod 1$, denote the rigid rotation by $\alpha$. Recall that every $f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})$ has a well-defined rotation number $\rho(f)\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

Fix real numbers $r\geq s\geq 0$. Define two subsets of the irrationals:
\[
\mathcal{C}_{r,s}=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}:\text{every }f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})\text{ with }\rho(f)\equiv\alpha\bmod 1\text{ is }C^s\text{-conjugate to }R_\alpha\},
\]
\[
\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}:\exists\,\varepsilon>0\text{ such that every }f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r_+(\mathbb{T})\text{ with }\rho(f)\equiv\alpha\bmod 1\text{ and }\|f-R_\alpha\|_{C^r}<\varepsilon\text{ is }C^s\text{-conjugate to }R_\alpha\}.
\]
Here "$C^s$-conjugate to $R_\alpha$" means there exists $h\in\mathrm{Diff}^s_+(\mathbb{T})$ with $h\circ f=R_\alpha\circ h$.

Determine the sets $\mathcal{C}_{r,s}$ and $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ explicitly in terms of arithmetic conditions on $\alpha$. Moreover, decide whether $\mathcal{C}_{r,s}=\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ in general, or whether the global and local arithmetic classes differ.
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the optimal arithmetic class for $C^s$-linearization of $C^r$ circle diffeomorphisms—both globally and in a neighborhood of rotations—remains an active and incompletely resolved problem. The Herman-Yoccoz theorem and subsequent work by Katznelson-Ornstein, Khanin-Teplinsky, and others yield essentially sharp results in some regularity ranges (e.g., Yoccoz's optimal Diophantine condition for analytic/smooth global conjugacy), but the exact arithmetic characterizations of $\mathcal{C}_{r,s}$ and $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{r,s}$ for all admissible $(r,s)$, and the precise comparison between the global and local classes, are not fully known.

status_evidence.title: Jean-Christophe Yoccoz and the theory of circle diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Arnold proved a local result... Arnold conjectured that the closeness to the rigid rotation is not necessary; this global version was proved by Herman almost two decades later.
status_evidence.claim: The distinction between local and global linearization theorems is a central, evolving question in the theory.

status_evidence.title: Smooth conjugacy classes of circle diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Herman and Yoccoz proved that if f is a C^r diffeomorphism with rotation number ρ Diophantine, |ρ-p/q|≥Cq^{-2-β}, 0≤β<1, and r>2β+1, then f is C^{r-1-β-ε}-conjugate to the rotation.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp arithmetic-regularity correspondences are known in restricted ranges but a full characterization of the classes $\mathcal{C}_{r,s}$ is not established.
